chapter_theme: Yama (இயமம்), the first limb: the Lord taught the four sages to keep the yamas in every direction even if the waters rise, and the man of yama is one who does not kill, lie or steal, is good and restrained, acts justly, shares his food, is stainless and free of drink and lust.

553.reading: 'Even if the waters rise and pour, in all eight directions keep the rich, cool yamas,' said the Lord with the cool coral-red matted hair, granting grace to the four who were absorbed in him.
553.nuance: The four (நால்வர்) are traditionally the sages Sanaka and the others taught by Siva as Dakshinamurti. எழுந்துநீர் பெய்யினும் may mean 'even if the flood comes', that is, whatever happens.

554.reading: One who does not kill, does not lie, does not steal, has good qualities, is good, has restraint, can act justly, shares before he eats, is stainless and has neither drink nor lust: he stands in yama.
554.nuance: The list gives ten marks, matching the ten yamas of the yoga texts. எண்குணன் may be 'one of eight qualities' or 'one of esteemed qualities'; in the Kural the same word names the Lord. நடுச்செய்ய வல்லான் is fairness, and பகுந்துண்பான் sharing one's food.

links.note: The Kural puts not killing first and not lying right behind it; Tirumular's list of yama opens in the same order, கொல்லான் then பொய் கூறான்.
Both name sharing one's food (பகுத்துண்டு, பகுந்துண்பான்) among the chief virtues; the Kural sets it beside protecting all life, Tirumular makes it part of the yogi's yama.
197 makes not killing the brightest flower in the worship of the guru; 554 puts it at the head of the yogi's restraints.
